currentAuthorizationModel.personaVisibilityFilter: Agent/SubAgent/Playbook call getToolDefinitions(persona.tools), which only limits definitions sent to the provider
currentAuthorizationModel.executionAuthority: src/tools/index.ts executeTool resolves any static or dynamic registered name and executes it without persona/session/capability validation
currentAuthorizationModel.supervisor: src/agent.ts calls approveToolCall only on the main Agent path; supervisor is disabled by default and approves dangerous tools when disabled or uninitialized
currentAuthorizationModel.sessionIdentity: Session has a private Link symbol for Link message origin only; tool execution has no session identity capability
currentAuthorizationModel.apiAuthentication: All /api routes require one local API token, but no per-operation capability or short-lived grant is enforced

bypassFindings.title: Persona tool lists are presentation filters, not execution authorization
Global dynamic registry permits same-name executor replacement without owner, version or session binding
SubAgent and Playbook execute global tools outside Supervisor
Supervisor is optional fail-open and can be disabled by the supervise tool
Persistent Terminal HTTP API directly starts and writes shell processes outside tool authorization
Persona has no immutable version or digest; old executors and switched sessions cannot be rejected at execution time
Malformed tool JSON is silently converted to empty arguments instead of failing schema validation
Parallel or stale runs share global Agent, Persona, Supervisor and dynamic tool state

frozenScopeForArchitecture: Immutable CapabilityContext containing session, persona identity/version, allowed tools/roots, network policy, risk class and approval grant reference
Execution-point authorization in the single tool dispatcher
Attenuated child contexts for SubAgent and Playbook
Dynamic tool registration identity and non-overridable ownership
Fail-closed behavior for missing, stale, cross-session or forged contexts
A controlled bridge for direct high-risk APIs such as Terminal
Attack tests proving zero executor invocation on denial
deferredToDependentCards: SEC-03 OS sandbox, environment/network/resource limits and complete process-tree termination
SEC-04 IPC migration, API token removal from query and short-lived user gesture grants
nonClaims: API token authentication is not equivalent to tool capability authorization.
A tool omitted from provider definitions is not proven unexecutable.
The existing Supervisor is advisory and cannot serve as the CapabilityBroker authority.
